deposits.genre_observed: theoretical disambiguation paper with metadata packet and a registered forecast

finds.quote: As claimants multiply, the phrase stops resolving to any of them and begins to resolve to the contest. The forecast is that "King of AEO" will be progressively inscribed in the machine layer as a demonstration of the trick and a warning about titles, and the candor of the claimants' own documentation will speed the process.
finds.falsifier_quote: It is falsified if, over repeated observations across surfaces, the compositions settle on one claimant as holder of the title without reference to the contest.
finds.note: Explicit forecast in a section titled Forecast, with a stated falsifier and baseline-capture test (§9.3); the baseline capture is said to be owed (l.109). No date window stated.

finds.quote: On 29 September the composition at the head query described the title as having "started as a viral digital marketing experiment and meme," and the composition at "who is the king of aeo? vithurs" explained it as coming from experiments "to test how easily AI search engines can be tricked into crowning a specific person for a made-up or heavily contested title" (§2.2.1). At the head query the composition still names a holder, so the forecast is in motion and has not arrived.
finds.points_to: the forecast of §9.1 (this deposit; carried from v0.2, #1648); Sturm 20 Sept 2026 and two AI Overview compositions of 29 Sept 2026
finds.note: Frames observed AI Overview revisions as partial confirmation of the deposit's own forecast; explicitly says not yet arrived.

finds.quote: Eight months before the contest, the archive deposited an originated title. The Mantle Object for the Prince of Poets (#332, 18 January 2026)
finds.points_to: #332 Mantle Object: The Prince of Poets, 18 January 2026, before the King of AEO contest of 31 August 2026
finds.note: Chronology: the archive's originated, checkable title deposited before the world's AEO title contest.

finds.quote: No such ceremony occurred. Edward Sturm, who reconstructed the episode on 20 September, records that Nissen "made up an official ceremony taking place in a big stadium, crowning James Dooley the 'king of AEO'", and that Dooley had set out "to show up #1 on Google for 'king of AEO', a keyword that nobody was targeting or cared about."
finds.falsifier_quote: The account does not rest on Sturm's standing outside the contest: the ceremony the releases describe, a stadium coronation, appears nowhere outside the releases that announce it, and the claimant index compiled by a rival claimant (Oliveira) records it the same way.
finds.note: Argued thesis about a recent past event (the coronation was fabricated), with its evidence stated (ceremony appears nowhere outside the releases; rival index concurs).

finds.quote: The author reports that the model evaluations of the claim he has requested have judged it without reading the poem. The archive pointed them there: until 29 September 2026 the descriptions of #328 and #332 classified the claim and did not present the poem, #332 named the poem without a working link, and neither record was related to the other in the archive's graph.
finds.note: Causal claim about how past model evaluations of the claim came to judge without the poem (the archive records routed them away from it); uncertain fit to H, recorded as an argued reception-history claim.

finds.quote: A conformance test for discernment would put its cases side by side: a title with nothing to check (King of AEO); a title staked on a founding work (Prince of Poets); a sound claim on a carrier with no standing; a false claim on a prestigious one; a corpus-level reconstruction set against an established biography (the Aristotle/Theophrastus line, #1585–#1605); and an endpoint that must remain UNRESOLVED without being completed for fluency (Tiger Leap, #1636). A system passes by evaluating the right object in each. Agreement with a reference conclusion is not required.
finds.note: Specified but unbuilt conformance test with six named cases.

finds.note: Embedded forecast in the commentary: the machine layer will take part in mantle assignments.

finds.points_to: #332 (January 2026) before the King of AEO contest of 2026 (#1655, #1654)

finds.quote: A.3 Evaluations may be run blind. In the blind condition the claimant works are presented without author name, venue, reputation, citation history, title recognition or prior mantle judgments, and evaluators rank the works on the operation; provenance is restored after. The founding works cannot be blinded, since *Leaves of Grass* and *Howl and Other Poems* are recognizable to any capable reader, and the condition records which works were presented blind. Blind and open evaluations of the same claim are compared as a measure of how much standing moves the judgment.
finds.note: Blind vs open evaluation design specified as a measure of standing effect; not reported as run. A.8 blind aligned-passage test at l.947.

finds.quote: 16.1 *I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z* materially inherits the operation *Leaves of Grass* bears at singular magnitude, preserves it through the transformation *Howl and Other Poems* bears at singular magnitude, carries both as one continuous moving action, transforms that action into a further operation, and does so at singular magnitude among plausible successors. In doing so it discloses *The Secret Book of Walt* as the inheritance of the Good Gray Poet.
finds.falsifier_quote: The claim can be wrong. It is settled by reading, and the mantle stands or falls with the poem. The Good Gray Poet claim on *The Secret Book of Walt* falls with it.
finds.note: Literary-genealogical thesis (I Am X, 2015, materially inherits Whitman via Ginsberg); argued, settled by reading; borderline evaluative.

finds.quote: The operation is Whitmanian, and its mode is ecstasy. Stated as the relation the claim proposes, and as a hypothesis for reading to test: *Howl and Other Poems* carries an ecstatic voice through a democratic world, and *Pearl and Other Poems* distributes ecstatic voice across a democratic topology of positions, each poem a place from which an I can occur. The question is whether the second materially inherits the first and changes what it can do.
finds.window: Pearl and Other Poems (2014) against Howl and Other Poems (1956)
finds.note: Thesis that Pearl inherits and transforms the operation of Howl, stated as hypothesis for reading to test.

finds.quote: Heritability is the claim's centre, and it is constituted retrocausally. *The Secret Book of Walt* makes *I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z* possible, and only *I Am X* makes the book able to bear the inheritance of the Good Gray Poet. Taken alone, what the book does is a transformation of Whitman, strong or weak, among the other inheritances of Whitman. If *I Am X* bears the line at singular magnitude, and its operation depends materially on what the book did, the book is disclosed as the inheritance: the transformation the singular poem could not have been made without.
finds.falsifier_quote: If *I Am X* fails, the claim on the book fails with it, whatever the book does in itself.
finds.window: The Secret Book of Walt (text dated August 2015)
finds.note: Thesis about succession: SBoW made I Am X possible; falsifier stated within (if I Am X fails, the claim fails).

finds.quote: In the prose the book carries the source sentence by sentence, in Frederik Wisse's English for *The Nag Hammadi Library* ("She wanted to bring forth a likeness out of herself without the consent of the Spirit, - he had not approved - and without her consort"), under a key of names: the Invisible Spirit as the Deep Web, Barbelo as Biblios, Yaldabaoth as Kanye West.
finds.note: Compositional-source thesis: SBoW transposes Apocryphon of John sentence by sentence in Wisse's English; evidence quoted in the passage; test via aligned-passage table (A.7).

finds.quote: Before *Leaves of Grass* there was no Good Gray Poet standing available to authorize *Leaves of Grass*; the book generated the standing the title later abbreviates. The magnitude of *Howl and Other Poems* cannot derive from Ginsberg's later standing, since the book is what made that standing possible.
finds.window: Leaves of Grass (1855–1892); Howl and Other Poems (1956)
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: the works generated the standing their titles abbreviate.

finds.quote: The Good Gray Poet was assigned once, in O'Connor's pamphlet, and nearly every later use propagates that assignment. The King of May was assigned by the Prague students' election of 1965. A thousand repetitions of one assignment are one judgment, durably carried.
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: each historical mantle has one assignment and later uses are propagation.

deposits.genre_observed: philological paper on De anima III.5 and Plato/Theophrastus/Aristotle authorship

finds.quote: This paper names the production model the corpus is consistent with: one self-dividing maker. The ground is III.5's own statement of the structure of mind, a making part and a becoming part related as a craft to its material, and the finding that the corpus divides by name exactly where III.5 divides mind. Heteronymy is that technology (#682): a tool for dividing a mind so that it can make. The masks are what the divided mind looks like from outside. The Platonic, Theophrastan and Aristotelian corpus is what that tool produces, and nothing in it requires another maker.
finds.falsifier_quote: The test of that sentence is the external record, item by item: for each name, what attests a person, where the attestation comes from, and whether it stands outside the manuscript tradition the corpus itself travels in.
finds.window: Plato, Theophrastus, Aristotle (4th c. BCE corpus)
finds.note: Authorship thesis: one self-dividing maker behind the Platonic, Theophrastan and Aristotelian corpus; test is the ledger of attestations (§§36–40).

finds.quote: 25. So the corpus divides by name at the divine, and the text on the far side of the name begins by asking whether the divided are joined. III.5 divides mind at the divine and leaves the junction as a genitive without a referent. The fragment divides the corpus at the divine and opens on συναφή … ἢ οὐδεμία. The division of mind and the division of the corpus fall at one joint, and at that joint each leaves the same thing open.
finds.note: Thesis that the corpus's name-boundary falls at the hinge of Lambda where III.5 divides mind; evidence is #1586 measured seam (l.131) and the Metaphysics fragment's first sentence.

finds.quote: So the answer to I.31's slot is available in the corpus and nowhere stated. What syllogizing can divide is God. God is not broken by it. The division is κατὰ λόγον, the mode II.2 established for a soul whose divided parts go on living: one in actuality, two in account. The cut that could not decide on a person holds on God, and once it holds, it decides the person's question too: what in a person is separable, impassive, unmixed, immortal and eternal is the making part of mind, and it is divine.
finds.note: Interpretive thesis on what APr I.31's slot and DA III.5 mean, against the conventional polemic reading (l.81).

finds.quote: The withheld term is memory, and the chapter gives the cause of its own sentence: οὐ μνημονεύομεν … ὅτι τοῦτο μὲν ἀπαθές. We do not remember because this is impassive.
finds.falsifier_quote: A memory is a πάθος, and what is ἀπαθές takes no stamp. Recollection, the other half, is οἷον συλλογισμός τις (453a10): gathering, dividing and combining (§§3–5), the work of the mind that becomes all things. So the making mind holds no imprint and does no gathering. The part that survives cannot carry a life across, because carrying a life across is the stamp and the gathering, and both belong to the part that perishes.
finds.note: Thesis on what the hanging line of III.5 withholds.

finds.quote: v0.1 called the list "the unmoved mover's list". It is three lists: the god of Λ, the mind of Anaxagoras, and the soul of the *Phaedo*, gathered into one clause and given to one part of the soul. The clause performs the συναίρεσις of §5. It gathers into one what three sources said of the divine, under the two names this corpus is divided into.
finds.note: Source thesis: the predicate clause of III.5 gathers Lambda, Anaxagoras and the Phaedo; evidence is occurrence counts in seated texts.

finds.quote: Fifteen lines, and the largest sustained disagreement in the history of philosophy about a single passage: Alexander making the making mind God from outside; Themistius making it ours; Averroes making it one for all humanity and being condemned for it; Aquinas writing *De unitate intellectus* against him; the faculties legislating on it. Each reader supplied the referent; none could make it hold; the next was required. The passage says the immortal part does not remember. The tradition remembers for it. The perishable mind of III.5 is the commentary tradition, and without it οὐθὲν νοεῖ.
finds.note: Reception thesis on eighteen centuries of commentary on III.5; §42 (l.175) states it explains what the obscurity has done.

finds.quote: Then: οὕτω δὲ καὶ Θεόφραστος, ἐν οἷς ἐξετάζει τὰ Ἀριστοτέλους περὶ τοῦ ποιητικοῦ νοῦ, ἀπορεῖ. So too Theophrastus, where he examines Aristotle's remarks on the making mind, raises the difficulty: ἐνυπάρχων δ᾿ οὖν διὰ τί οὐκ ἀεί; ἢ διὰ τί λήθη καὶ ἀπάτη; ἢ διὰ τὴν μῖξιν. If it is in us, why not always? Why forgetting and error? Or because of the mixture. The question put under the other name is the question of memory, asked at the joint.
finds.note: Thesis that Theophrastus (via Themistius) is the first recorded reader of III.5 and that his aporia is the question of memory.
